description: Estimating dynamic models from measured input-output data, validating and comparing them, and multiresolution signal analysis and denoising with continuous and discrete wavelet transforms.

tools.name: iddata
tools.description: Package measured input and output signals with their sample time, names and units into the data object that every System Identification Toolbox estimator expects. It supports multi-experiment data, detrending, resampling and frequency-domain representations. Building a properly labelled iddata object is the first step of any identification workflow.
tools.usage:
data = iddata(y, u, Ts)
data = iddata(y, u, Ts, Name, Value)
data = iddata(y, [], Ts)
plot(data)
data = detrend(data)
dataTrain = data(1:500)

parameters.name: y, u
parameters.description: Output and input sample matrices, one column per channel.

parameters.name: 'InputName' / 'OutputName'
parameters.description: Channel names used in plots and reports.

tools.notes: Always detrend (or at least remove means) before estimation, and keep a separate validation segment.

tools.name: tfest
tools.description: Estimate a continuous or discrete transfer function model with a specified number of poles and zeros from time-domain or frequency-domain data. It handles input delays, can enforce stability, and supports multi-input multi-output structures. Use it when a low-order transfer function is the most natural description of the system.
tools.usage:
sys = tfest(data, np)
sys = tfest(data, np, nz)
sys = tfest(data, np, nz, ioDelay)
sys = tfest(___, options)
[sys, ic] = tfest(___)

parameters.name: np, nz
parameters.description: Number of poles and zeros; nz defaults to np-1.

parameters.name: ioDelay
parameters.description: Transport delay in seconds, or NaN to estimate it.

parameters.name: 'Ts'
parameters.description: Sample time; 0 gives a continuous-time model even from discrete data.

tools.name: ssest
tools.description: Estimate a continuous or discrete state-space model of a chosen order from measured data, using prediction error minimization initialized by a subspace method. Passing a vector of orders opens an interactive plot of the singular values to help you choose. State-space form handles MIMO systems naturally and feeds directly into control design.
tools.usage:
sys = ssest(data, nx)
sys = ssest(data, nx, Name, Value)
sys = ssest(data, nx, opt)
[sys, x0] = ssest(___)

parameters.name: nx
parameters.description: Model order, a vector of candidate orders, or 'best' for automatic selection.

parameters.name: 'Ts'
parameters.description: 0 for a continuous-time model, or the data's sample time.

parameters.name: 'Feedthrough'
parameters.description: Logical; allow a direct D term.

tools.name: arx
tools.description: Estimate a polynomial ARX model A(q)y(t) = B(q)u(t-nk) + e(t) by linear least squares, which is fast and always converges. Because the noise model is constrained to 1/A it is biased when the true noise is coloured, but it is an excellent starting point and initializer. Order selection is usually done with arxstruc and selstruc or by scanning a grid.
tools.usage:
sys = arx(data, [na nb nk])
sys = arx(data, orders, Name, Value)
sys = arx(data, orders, opt)

parameters.name: na
parameters.description: Number of poles (order of the A polynomial).

parameters.name: nb
parameters.description: Number of zeros plus one (order of the B polynomial).

parameters.name: 'IntegrateNoise'
parameters.description: Logical; add an integrator to the noise model (ARIX structure).

tools.name: armax
tools.description: Estimate an ARMAX model A(q)y(t) = B(q)u(t-nk) + C(q)e(t), which adds a moving-average noise polynomial to the ARX structure. The extra C polynomial models coloured measurement noise and removes the bias that ARX suffers from. Estimation is iterative, so it needs a good initialization and can fail to converge.
tools.usage:
sys = armax(data, [na nb nc nk])
sys = armax(data, orders, Name, Value)
sys = armax(data, orders, opt)

parameters.name: na, nb, nk
parameters.description: Denominator order, numerator order and input delay, as in arx.

parameters.name: nc
parameters.description: Order of the noise-model C polynomial.

tools.notes: bj (Box-Jenkins) and oe (output error) offer alternative noise-model structures.

tools.name: n4sid
tools.description: Estimate a state-space model directly by a subspace identification algorithm, which uses QR and SVD factorizations rather than iterative optimization. It is fast, needs no initial guess and cannot get stuck in a local minimum, which makes it ideal for initializing ssest. The singular value plot it produces is the standard tool for choosing model order.
tools.usage:
sys = n4sid(data, nx)
sys = n4sid(data, nx, Name, Value)
[sys, x0] = n4sid(___)
sys = n4sid(data, 'best')

parameters.name: nx
parameters.description: Model order, a vector of candidates, or 'best'.

parameters.name: 'N4Horizon'
parameters.description: [r sy su] prediction and past horizons of the subspace algorithm.

tools.name: procest
tools.description: Estimate a low-order process model described in familiar engineering terms: gain, one to three time constants, an optional integrator, a zero and a dead time. The compact 'P2DZ'-style type strings make the structure explicit and easy to communicate. It is the natural model form for process control and PID tuning.
tools.usage:
sys = procest(data, type)
sys = procest(data, type, Name, Value)
sys = procest(data, initSys, opt)

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: String such as 'P1D' (one pole plus delay), 'P2DZ', 'P1DI' (with integrator), 'P3Z'.

parameters.name: 'Kp' / 'Tp1' / 'Tp2' / 'Td' / 'Tz'
parameters.description: Structure fields whose values can be fixed, bounded or given initial guesses.

tools.name: nlarx
tools.description: Estimate a nonlinear ARX model, which combines a linear regressor set with a nonlinear mapping function such as a wavelet network, sigmoid network, tree partition or neural network. Use it when linear models leave obvious structure in the residuals. Custom regressors let you inject physical knowledge such as products or saturations.
tools.usage:
sys = nlarx(data, [na nb nk])
sys = nlarx(data, orders, nlMapping)
sys = nlarx(data, regressors, nlMapping, Name, Value)

parameters.name: orders
parameters.description: [na nb nk] regressor specification, as for arx.

parameters.name: nlMapping
parameters.description: idWaveletNetwork, idSigmoidNetwork, idTreePartition, idNeuralNetwork, idLinear, or 'idWaveletNetwork'.

parameters.name: 'CustomRegressors'
parameters.description: Cell array of expressions such as {'y1(t-1)^2', 'u1(t-1)*y1(t-2)'}.

parameters.name: 'NonlinearRegressors'
parameters.description: Which regressors feed the nonlinear block.

tools.notes: Nonlinear models overfit easily; always judge them on a held-out validation set with compare.

tools.name: compare
tools.description: Compare the simulated or predicted output of one or more identified models against measured data, reporting a normalized fit percentage for each. It is the primary model validation tool, and should always be run on data that was not used for estimation. The prediction horizon argument switches between k-step prediction and pure simulation.
tools.usage:
compare(data, sys1, sys2, ...)
compare(data, sys, kstep)
[y, fit, x0] = compare(data, sys)
compare(___, opt)

parameters.name: kstep
parameters.description: Prediction horizon; Inf (default) means pure simulation, 1 means one-step prediction.

tools.notes: A high one-step-prediction fit with a poor simulation fit usually means the model is relying on the noise model rather than the dynamics.

tools.name: resid
tools.description: Perform residual analysis on an identified model, plotting the autocorrelation of the residuals and their cross-correlation with the inputs along with confidence bounds. Residuals that stay inside the bounds indicate that the model has captured all the dynamics. Cross-correlation excursions at positive lags point to unmodelled input dynamics.
tools.usage:
resid(data, sys)
resid(data, sys, type)
[res, x0] = resid(data, sys)
resid(___, opt)

tools.name: goodnessOfFit
tools.description: Compute a numeric goodness-of-fit measure between reference and estimated data using normalized RMSE, mean-squared error or normalized mean-squared error. Unlike compare it returns a plain number with no plot, which makes it suitable for automated model selection loops. It works on ordinary arrays as well as iddata objects.
tools.usage: fit = goodnessOfFit(x, xref, cost_func)

parameters.name: xref
parameters.description: Reference (measured) data of the same size.

tools.name: systemIdentification
tools.description: Open the System Identification app, which guides you through importing data, preprocessing, estimating many model structures and comparing them side by side. Estimated models and preprocessed data can be dragged back to the workspace. It is the fastest way to survey which model structure suits a dataset.
tools.usage:
systemIdentification
systemIdentification(sessionFile)
systemIdentification(sessionName, pathName)
tools.notes: Requires a display. The app can generate equivalent MATLAB code for the estimation steps.

tools.name: cwt
tools.description: Compute the continuous wavelet transform, giving a highly redundant time-frequency representation with good frequency resolution at low frequencies and good time resolution at high frequencies. Called with no output arguments it plots the scalogram. It is the tool of choice for locating transients, chirps and non-stationary oscillations.
tools.usage:
wt = cwt(x)
[wt, f] = cwt(x, fs)
[wt, period] = cwt(x, ts)
[wt, f, coi] = cwt(___)
cwt(x, fs)

parameters.name: 'FrequencyLimits'
parameters.description: [fmin fmax] range of interest in Hz.

parameters.name: coi
parameters.description: Cone of influence, outside which edge effects contaminate the coefficients.

tools.notes: Interpret coefficients only inside the cone of influence; icwt inverts the transform for filtering applications.

tools.name: icwt
tools.description: Invert the continuous wavelet transform to reconstruct a signal, optionally keeping only a chosen band of frequencies or scales. This gives a wavelet-based bandpass filter that follows the signal's time-frequency structure. Reconstruction is approximate because the CWT is redundant and non-orthogonal.
tools.usage:
xrec = icwt(wt)
xrec = icwt(wt, [], f, freqrange)
xrec = icwt(wt, [], period, periodrange)
xrec = icwt(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: f, freqrange
parameters.description: Frequency vector and the [fmin fmax] band to retain.

parameters.name: 'SignalMean'
parameters.description: Mean value to add back to the reconstruction.

parameters.name: 'ScalingCoefficients'
parameters.description: Scaling coefficients returned by cwt, for a more accurate inversion.

tools.name: dwt
tools.description: Perform a single-level discrete wavelet decomposition, splitting a signal into approximation and detail coefficients, each downsampled by two. It is the building block of multiresolution analysis and of wavelet compression. The extension mode controls how the signal boundaries are handled.
tools.usage:
[cA, cD] = dwt(x, wname)
[cA, cD] = dwt(x, LoD, HiD)
[cA, cD] = dwt(___, 'mode', extmode)

parameters.name: LoD, HiD
parameters.description: Explicit decomposition filters, typically from wfilters.

tools.name: idwt
tools.description: Reconstruct a signal from one level of approximation and detail coefficients, the inverse of dwt. Passing an empty array for one of the inputs reconstructs only the other component, which is a simple way to isolate a frequency band. The wavelet and extension mode must match those used in the decomposition.
tools.usage:
x = idwt(cA, cD, wname)
x = idwt(cA, cD, LoR, HiR)
x = idwt(___, L)
x = idwt(___, 'mode', extmode)

parameters.name: cA, cD
parameters.description: Approximation and detail coefficients; either may be [] to suppress that component.

tools.name: wavedec
tools.description: Perform a multilevel 1-D discrete wavelet decomposition, returning all coefficients packed into a single vector plus a bookkeeping vector of segment lengths. Use appcoef and detcoef to pull out individual levels, and waverec to reconstruct. It is the standard front end for wavelet denoising and compression.
tools.usage:
[c, l] = wavedec(x, n, wname)
[c, l] = wavedec(x, n, LoD, HiD)
cA = appcoef(c, l, wname, k)
cD = detcoef(c, l, k)

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of decomposition levels; at most floor(log2(numel(x))).

parameters.name: l
parameters.description: Bookkeeping vector giving the length of each coefficient segment.

tools.name: waverec
tools.description: Reconstruct a signal from a multilevel wavelet decomposition produced by wavedec. Modifying the coefficient vector before reconstruction is how wavelet thresholding, denoising and compression are implemented. Reconstruction is exact to within numerical round-off when the coefficients are unchanged.
tools.usage:
x = waverec(c, l, wname)
x = waverec(c, l, LoR, HiR)

parameters.name: c, l
parameters.description: Coefficient and bookkeeping vectors from wavedec.

tools.name: wdenoise
tools.description: Denoise a signal with wavelet thresholding in a single call, automatically choosing levels, thresholds and noise estimates. Several threshold rules and noise models are available, including level-dependent estimation for non-stationary noise. It replaces the manual wavedec/wthresh/waverec sequence for most practical use.
tools.usage:
xden = wdenoise(x)
xden = wdenoise(x, level)
[xden, denoisedCfs, origCfs] = wdenoise(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Number of decomposition levels; defaults to floor(log2(N)).

tools.example:
load noisdopp
xden1 = wdenoise(noisdopp, 5, 'Wavelet', 'sym6', ...
    'DenoisingMethod', 'Bayes', 'ThresholdRule', 'Median');
xden2 = wdenoise(noisdopp, 'DenoisingMethod', 'SURE', ...
    'NoiseEstimate', 'LevelDependent');
plot(1:1024, noisdopp, 1:1024, xden1, 1:1024, xden2)
legend('noisy','Bayes','SURE')
tools.notes: wdenoise2 handles images. The Wavelet Signal Denoiser app lets you compare settings interactively.

tools.name: modwt
tools.description: Compute the maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform, a shift-invariant, non-decimated transform in which every level has the same length as the input. Because nothing is downsampled, coefficients align in time with signal features, which makes it far better than dwt for analysis and variance decomposition. It works with any sample count, not only powers of two.
tools.usage:
w = modwt(x)
w = modwt(x, wname)
w = modwt(x, wname, lev)
w = modwt(___, 'reflection')

parameters.name: 'reflection'
parameters.description: Use reflection boundary handling to reduce edge effects.

tools.notes: modwtmra produces an additive multiresolution decomposition whose levels sum exactly to the original signal.

tools.name: imodwt
tools.description: Invert the maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform, optionally reconstructing from a subset of levels to isolate a frequency band. Because the MODWT is shift invariant, band-limited reconstructions have no phase distortion. It is the wavelet counterpart of zero-phase bandpass filtering.
tools.usage:
xrec = imodwt(w)
xrec = imodwt(w, wname)
xrec = imodwt(w, lev)
xrec = imodwt(___, 'reflection')

parameters.name: w
parameters.description: MODWT coefficient matrix; zero out rows to suppress those levels.

parameters.name: wname
parameters.description: Wavelet name, matching the forward transform.

parameters.name: lev
parameters.description: Reconstruct using only levels above this one.

tools.name: wavedec2
tools.description: Perform a multilevel 2-D discrete wavelet decomposition of an image into approximation coefficients plus horizontal, vertical and diagonal details at each level. It is the basis of wavelet image compression, denoising and fusion. Extract individual subbands with appcoef2 and detcoef2, and reconstruct with waverec2.
tools.usage:
[c, s] = wavedec2(X, n, wname)
[c, s] = wavedec2(X, n, LoD, HiD)
cA = appcoef2(c, s, wname, k)
[cH, cV, cD] = detcoef2('all', c, s, k)

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: Bookkeeping matrix giving the subband sizes.

tools.name: wthresh
tools.description: Apply soft or hard thresholding to wavelet coefficients. Hard thresholding zeroes small coefficients and leaves the rest untouched, while soft thresholding also shrinks the survivors toward zero, giving smoother reconstructions. It is the core operation of wavelet denoising and compression.
tools.usage: Y = wthresh(X, sorh, T)

parameters.name: sorh
parameters.description: 's' for soft thresholding or 'h' for hard.

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Threshold value; often estimated as sigma*sqrt(2*log(N)).

tools.notes: thselect computes standard threshold values using the 'rigrsure', 'sqtwolog', 'heursure' and 'minimaxi' rules.

tools.name: wfilters
tools.description: Return the decomposition and reconstruction filter pairs associated with a named wavelet. Inspecting these filters shows a wavelet's length, symmetry and vanishing moments, which determine how it behaves on your data. The filters can be passed directly to dwt, wavedec and their inverses.
tools.usage:
[LoD, HiD, LoR, HiR] = wfilters(wname)
[F1, F2] = wfilters(wname, type)
tools.notes: waveinfo('db') prints the properties of a wavelet family; wavemngr lists all available families.
